legend: Let's call two strings s%%ZSMJ0%% and t%%ZSMJ1%% anagrams of each other if it is possible to rearrange symbols in the string s%%ZSMJ2%% to get a string, equal to t%%ZSMJ3%%.

Let's consider two strings s%%ZSMJ4%% and t%%ZSMJ5%% which are anagrams of each other. We say that t%%ZSMJ6%% is a reducible anagram of s%%ZSMJ7%% if there exists an integer k≥2%%ZSMJ8%% and 2k%%ZSMJ9%% non-empty strings s1,t1,s2,t2,…,sk,tk%%ZSMJ10%% that satisfy the following conditions:
If we write the strings s1,s2,…,sk%%ZSMJ11%% in order, the resulting string will be equal to s%%ZSMJ12%%;
If we write the strings t1,t2,…,tk%%ZSMJ13%% in order, the resulting string will be equal to t%%ZSMJ14%%;
For all integers i%%ZSMJ15%% between 1%%ZSMJ16%% and k%%ZSMJ17%% inclusive, si%%ZSMJ18%% and ti%%ZSMJ19%% are anagrams of each other.

If such strings don't exist, then t%%ZSMJ20%% is said to be an irreducible anagram of s%%ZSMJ21%%. Note that these notions are only defined when s%%ZSMJ22%% and t%%ZSMJ23%% are anagrams of each other.

For example, consider the string s=%%ZSMJ24%% "gamegame". Then the string t=%%ZSMJ25%% "megamage" is a reducible anagram of s%%ZSMJ26%%, we may choose for example s1=%%ZSMJ27%% "game", s2=%%ZSMJ28%% "gam", s3=%%ZSMJ29%% "e" and t1=%%ZSMJ30%% "mega", t2=%%ZSMJ31%% "mag", t3=%%ZSMJ32%% "e":
On the other hand, we can prove that t=%%ZSMJ33%% "memegaga" is an irreducible anagram of s%%ZSMJ34%%.

You will be given a string s%%ZSMJ35%% and q%%ZSMJ36%% queries, represented by two integers 1≤l≤r≤|s|%%ZSMJ37%% (where |s|%%ZSMJ38%% is equal to the length of the string s%%ZSMJ39%%). For each query, you should find if the substring of s%%ZSMJ40%% formed by characters from the l%%ZSMJ41%%-th to the r%%ZSMJ42%%-th has at least one irreducible anagram.
input: The first line contains a string s%%ZSMJ43%%, consisting of lowercase English characters (1≤|s|≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ44%%).
The second line contains a single integer q%%ZSMJ45%% (1≤q≤105%%ZSMJ46%%)  — the number of queries.

Each of the following q%%ZSMJ47%% lines contain two integers l%%ZSMJ48%% and r%%ZSMJ49%% (1≤l≤r≤|s|%%ZSMJ50%%), representing a query for the substring of s%%ZSMJ51%% formed by characters from the l%%ZSMJ52%%-th to the r%%ZSMJ53%%-th.
output: For each query, print a single line containing "Yes" (without quotes) if the corresponding substring has at least one irreducible anagram, and a single line containing "No" (without quotes) otherwise.
note: In the first sample, in the first and third queries, the substring is "a", which has itself as an irreducible anagram since two or more non-empty strings cannot be put together to obtain "a". On the other hand, in the second query, the substring is "aaa", which has no irreducible anagrams: its only anagram is itself, and we may choose s1=%%ZSMJ54%% "a", s2=%%ZSMJ55%% "aa", t1=%%ZSMJ56%% "a", t2=%%ZSMJ57%% "aa" to show that it is a reducible anagram.
In the second query of the second sample, the substring is "abb", which has, for example, "bba" as an irreducible anagram.
